learningObjectives: Define what a Verification Attribute is.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Scenario: A New SUT Feature to Verify

elements.text: The SUT (built with Agile) added a new feature: after clicking Add to Cart with a chosen quantity, a message appears — green/success for a positive whole number, red/error for a negative one. You already have Modules, Template, TestCases, and TemplateInstances from the previous version; you now receive an updated TestSheet with new Verification Attributes to test this message.

elements.description: A new type of Attribute — shown in green — that is NOT an input to the SUT. Instead, it holds a value Tosca compares against the SUT's actual output. If the two values match once entered into the TestCase, the verification succeeds; otherwise it fails.

elements.text: In the new TestSheet, the Quantity Attribute has 2 Instances: +4 (valid) and -4 (invalid). For +4, the Verification Attribute checks for the message "The product has been added to your shopping cart"; for -4, it checks for "Quantity should be positive". After modifying the Template and Instantiating, this produces 2 TestCases that validate the system message.

elements.title: Modification workflow
items: Check the Template for any References to resolve BEFORE modifying it, so changes don't feed through to the shared Library.
Identify all TestSteps that need modification, and add any new steps required to verify the new message(s).
Link the new, revised TestSheet to the Template — linking a new TestSheet automatically removes the link to the old one.
Check the XL links: if Attributes/Instances are named identically in both old and new TestSheets, Tosca updates the links automatically — but verify them carefully.
Manually add any brand-new links (like the Verification Values) to their respective TestStepValues.
Run Check Template again to catch missed or forgotten links.
Delete the OLD TemplateInstance folder before instantiating with the new TestSheet.

elements.text: Changes and new values are NOT reflected in existing TemplateInstances until you Instantiate again. Skipping this step means your 'updated' TestCases still run on old data.

A TestStepValue can only hold one link at a time. Before linking a NEW Attribute to a TestStepValue that's already linked to a different Attribute, you must first delete the existing Value — otherwise the new link won't take.

rows: Test Design Specialist provided a brand-new TestSheet
Link the new TestSheet (removes old link) → delete the old TemplateInstance folder → Instantiate (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I).
Test Design Specialist amended the EXISTING TestSheet (same file, new rows/values)
Modify the Template if needed → use Re-Instantiate — it refreshes existing TemplateInstances AND adds any new ones, without deleting anything manually.

elements.text: Re-Instantiate can be run by right-clicking the TemplateInstance folder → ReInstantiate. It's the safer, additive option when the underlying TestSheet was just updated rather than replaced.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting to (re)instantiate after modifying a Template
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates update a Template's links and TestSteps but never re-run instantiation, then wonder why the TestCases still show old behavior.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Modifications only reach the TestCasesInstances after Instantiation (new TestSheet) or Re-Instantiation (amended TestSheet).

examPitfalls.title: Not deleting the old TemplateInstance folder before a new TestSheet link
examPitfalls.trapDescription: When replacing the TestSheet entirely, learners instantiate without removing the previous TemplateInstance folder, leading to duplicate/stale TestCases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When linking a completely NEW TestSheet, delete the old TemplateInstance folder before Instantiating. Re-Instantiate is only for an amended (same) TestSheet.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an Attribute is a Verification Attribute by default
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates confuse a normal input Attribute with a Verification Attribute.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Verification Attribute is shown in GREEN and is compared against the SUT's actual output, not fed in as input.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to re-link a TestStepValue without clearing the old value first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates drag a new Attribute onto a TestStepValue that's already linked to a different Attribute, and the new link doesn't take (or silently conflicts).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A TestStepValue holds only one link at a time. Delete the existing Value first, then drag the new Attribute onto the now-empty TestStepValue.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What color is a Verification Attribute shown in, and what is its purpose?

options.text: Blue — it indicates the Attribute belongs to a Template.
Red — it marks an Attribute as required.
Verification Attributes have no distinct color; they're identical to regular Attributes.
Green — its value is compared against the SUT's actual output rather than being fed in as an input.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same color used for 'success' states in many UIs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Verification Attribute is shown in green. Its value is used by Tosca to verify the SUT's output — not as input data — and the TestCase step succeeds only if the two values match.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You link a brand-new TestSheet (replacing the old one) to an existing Template. What must you do before Instantiating?

options.text: Delete the old TemplateInstance folder first.
Nothing extra — Instantiate always overwrites old TemplateInstances automatically.
Rename the Template.
Convert the Template back to a TestCase first.

practiceQuiz.hint: This step is different from a Re-Instantiate scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When replacing the TestSheet entirely, you must delete the old TemplateInstance folder before Instantiating, to avoid duplicate or stale TestCases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Test Design Specialist just added 2 new rows to the SAME existing TestSheet (didn't replace the file). What is the correct next action?

options.text: Nothing needs to be done since the TestSheet wasn't replaced.
Use Re-Instantiate — it refreshes existing TemplateInstances and adds new ones.
Delete the entire TemplateInstance folder and Instantiate from scratch.
Manually create the 2 new TestCases by hand.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the safer, additive option for an amended (not replaced) TestSheet.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Re-Instantiate is designed for exactly this case: an amended existing TestSheet. It refreshes data in existing TemplateInstances and adds any new ones without manual deletion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When you link a new TestSheet to a Template that already had one linked, what happens to the old link?

options.text: It's automatically removed when the new TestSheet is linked.
The Template becomes invalid and must be recreated.
The old TestSheet link must be manually removed first, or the Template will error.
Both TestSheets remain linked simultaneously.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Linking a new TestSheet automatically removes the link to the previous one — a Template can only have one linked TestSheet at a time.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestStepValue is already linked to the Attribute 'Email'. You now want to link it instead to a new Attribute, 'Value - Email', from an updated TestSheet. What must you do first?

options.text: Delete and recreate the entire TestStep.
Nothing — dragging the new Attribute automatically replaces the old link.
Rename the TestStepValue first.
Delete the existing Value from the TestStepValue, then drag the new Attribute onto it.

practiceQuiz.hint: A TestStepValue can only hold one link at a time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestStepValue holds only one link at a time. Before linking a new Attribute to a TestStepValue that already has a value from a different Attribute, you must delete the existing Value first — otherwise the new link won't take.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct process to link a TestSheet to a Template?

options.text: Right click on the Template, select Instantiation, choose the TestSheet.
Drag and drop the TestSheet onto the Template.
Right click on the TestSheet and select the correct Template from the list.
Drag the TestSheet and drop it onto the TemplateInstances.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a direct drag-and-drop action between the two objects, not a menu selection.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You link a TestSheet to a Template by dragging it from the TestCaseDesign section and dropping it directly onto the Template in the TestCase section — not via Instantiation, a TestSheet-side menu, or the TemplateInstances folder.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Is it necessary to Instantiate a Template?

options.text: No, I can link a Template to an ExecutionList and the {XL[ ]} References are translated during runtime.
Yes, because {XL[ ]} References are only translated during Instantiation.
Yes, because you link the Template to a TestSheet during Instantiation.
No, this is done automatically by Tosca during runtime.

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall: 'a Template cannot be run as a test itself' — it needs one more step first.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Yes, Instantiation is required. A Template cannot be run as a TestCase on its own — its {XL[ ]} References only get translated into actual, usable values when the Template is Instantiated, which is what produces the real, runnable TestCases in the TemplateInstance folder.

quickRecap.value: Green Attribute — its value is checked against the SUT's actual output, not used as input.
Resolve refs → edit/add TestSteps → link new TestSheet → verify XL links → add new links manually → Check Template.
Delete old TemplateInstance folder → Instantiate (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I).
Use Re-Instantiate — refreshes + adds instances, no manual deletion.
If Attribute/Instance names match old vs new TestSheet, Tosca updates XL links automatically — but verify.
Delete the existing Value first — a TestStepValue holds only one link at a time.
